Techniques Used: Analytical modeling using power flow equations
Bessel function analysis for inverter output voltage
Influence Modeling (Cascading and Linear Threshold Models)
Data & Platforms: Full-bridge inverter with Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation (SPWM)
Application Areas: Resilience of Electrical Grids with High Penetration Inverter-Based Renewables
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Data-Driven Nonlinear System Identification: Utilizing Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) combined with Volterra-based Nonlinearity Index (VNI) to distinguish between linearizable terms and higher-order nonlinear dynamics in power systems, revealing a shift from module-level to system-level nonlinearity in inverter-based resources.

Hybrid Dynamical Systems Analysis: Integrating SINDy with the Hankel Alternative View of Koopman (HAVOK) framework to detect and analyze complex, coupled multi-scale nonlinear dynamics, enabling robust model identification where generic sparse regression fails to capture second-order nonlinearities.

Topological Harmonic Cancellation: Leveraging grid topology configuration to induce phase shifts that facilitate self-compensation among inverters, achieving significant harmonic reduction through system-level structural adjustments rather than component-level filtering.

Interdependent Network Resilience Modeling: Synthesizing epidemiological (SIR) and influence models with network optimization to quantify risks from weaponized disinformation, analyzing how misinformation manipulates user behavior to indirectly disrupt physical critical infrastructure layers.

Sparse Regression for Model Discovery: Applying L1 regularization and compressed sensing techniques to extract parsimonious mathematical models from high-dimensional time-series data, such as voltage time histories, to identify governing equations of nonlinear energy flows.
Summary Description: John Jiang specializes in the intersection of power systems engineering, nonlinear dynamics, and critical infrastructure resilience. His research primarily focuses on characterizing and mitigating complex nonlinear behaviors in electrical grids with high penetrations of inverter-based renewable resources. By employing advanced data-driven techniques like Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) and HAVOK, he quantifies system-level nonlinearity and develops topological strategies for harmonic cancellation. Beyond physical systems, Jiang extends his expertise to cyber-physical resilience, modeling how disinformation campaigns can disrupt interdependent networks like transportation and supply chains. His work bridges theoretical control theory with practical applications in grid stability, power quality, and national security, providing quantitative tools for managing the vulnerabilities of modern critical infrastructure.
